To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there were no statistical difference between the number of verbalizations of frustration by condition; (2) there were no differences in the number or types of usability problems found by condition; (3) there were no difference in the number of positive comments by conditions; and (4) there were no significant differences in the number and types of problems found by condition.
the number of verbalizations of frustrations and positive comments by condition did not differ.
the three think-aloud protocols did not differ from each other with respect to the number of verbalizations by participants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
how think-aloud protocols affect the number of verbal and non-verbal expressions of frustration and positive comments that participants express when they use an information-rich Web application.
how the think-aloud protocols are being used to analyze usability problems in a Web site.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study did not find any significant difference between the conditions.
the study did not show any significant differences between the three conditions with respect to verbalization.
the use of think alouds in usability testing of information-rich Web sites should be done with caution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that think-aloud protocols are a valuable tool for understanding user behavior.
the use of think aloud protocols in the usability testing of an informational-rich Web site does not appear to be a good idea, as the results are inconclusive.
the use of think aloud protocols in a usability study does not necessarily provide the most useful information to the researcher.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the number of counts of verbalized and/or non-verbalized comments of frustrations or positive comments by condition does not provide enough information to determine if any of the conditions lead to a better or worse understanding of the usability issues associated with the site.
the number of verbalizations of frustration by condition does not provide a sufficient measure of usability for an information-rich Web page.
the number of verbalizations of frustration or positive comments by condition alone cannot be the sole measure to determine whether a particular type of think-aloud protocol is better than another.
